'''Bobby Henderson''' is an American satirist and activist, known for being the founder of [[Pastafarianism]], a parody religion.

==Early life and education==
Henderson was born on July 18, 1980, in [[Roseburg, Oregon]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.spaghettimonster.org/about/ |title=About « Church of the Flying Spaghetti Monster |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200113104934/https://www.spaghettimonster.org/about/ |archive-date=January 13, 2020}}</ref> He studied physics at [[Oregon State University]].<ref name="Timms2019">{{Cite news |last=Timms |first=Peter |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/may/18/pasta-strainers-and-pirates-how-the-church-of-the-flying-spaghetti-monster-was-born |title=Pasta strainers and pirates: how the Church of the Flying Spaghetti Monster was born |date=May 17, 2019 |work=The Guardian |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191116235547/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/may/18/pasta-strainers-and-pirates-how-the-church-of-the-flying-spaghetti-monster-was-born |archive-date=November 16, 2019}}</ref>

==Pastafarianism==
{{main|Flying Spaghetti Monster}}
In 2005, Henderson founded the religion of Pastafarianism in response to the [[Kansas evolution hearings|Kansas State Board of Education's decision]] to teach [[intelligent design]] alongside evolution in schools.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Natanson |first=Hannah |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2019/09/20/pastafarian-opened-council-meeting-wearing-spaghetti-strainer-he-says-its-about-separation-church-state/ |title=A Pastafarian opened a council meeting wearing a spaghetti strainer. He says it's about separation of church and state. |date=September 20, 2019 |newspaper=The Washington Post |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921001953/https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2019/09/20/pastafarian-opened-council-meeting-wearing-spaghetti-strainer-he-says-its-about-separation-church-state/ |archive-date=September 21, 2019}}</ref> He requested that "Pastafarianism" be taught alongside intelligent design and "logical conjecture based on overwhelming observable evidence".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Millhiser |first=Ian |url=https://www.vox.com/2019/9/22/20875562/separation-church-state-pastafarian-satanic-temple-establishment-flying-spaghetti-monster |title=A Pastafarian hilariously trolled a town council meeting. The stakes are profoundly serious. |date=September 22, 2019 |work=Vox |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216072746/https://www.vox.com/2019/9/22/20875562/separation-church-state-pastafarian-satanic-temple-establishment-flying-spaghetti-monster |archive-date=December 16, 2019 |language=en}}</ref> After his protest letter to the board was ignored, he posted it online and the beliefs quickly gained traction.<ref name=Timms2019/>

In 2006, he wrote ''[[The Gospel of the Flying Spaghetti Monster]]'',<ref>{{Cite news |last=Slisco |first=Aila |url=https://www.newsweek.com/pastafarian-pastor-praises-flying-spaghetti-monster-government-sponsored-prayer-session-alaska-1460109 |title=Pastor from the Church of the Flying Spaghetti Monster led "Pastafarian prayers" at a government meeting in Alaska |date=September 19, 2019 |work=Newsweek |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200204111432/https://www.newsweek.com/pastafarian-pastor-praises-flying-spaghetti-monster-government-sponsored-prayer-session-alaska-1460109 |archive-date=February 4, 2020 |language=en}}</ref> a book detailing the core beliefs of the religion.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Henley |first=Jon |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/aug/16/pastafarianism-is-not-a-religion-dutch-court-rules |title=Spaghetti injunction: Pastafarianism is not a religion, Dutch court rules |date=August 16, 2018 |work=The Guardian |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190919214250/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/aug/16/pastafarianism-is-not-a-religion-dutch-court-rules |archive-date=September 19, 2019}}</ref> He suggested that all the proceedings from the book would go into building a (tax-free) pirate ship that would travel the world and spread the gospel about Pastafarianism, "like a floating church".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Craig |first=Kathleen |title=Passion of the Spaghetti Monster |url=https://www.wired.com/2005/12/passion-of-the-spaghetti-monster/ |access-date=2025-10-06 |work=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref>

In 2019, Henderson repeated his belief that religion should be kept out of government schools and money kept out of religion.<ref name=Timms2019/>
